subject: Audit trace export: delivery options & retention boundaries
messages:
From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@finvero.co>
To: hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
Cc: security@finvero.co
Date: 2026-12-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Audit trace export: formats / retention / deletion proof

Hi Hiro,

We're preparing our audit packet for an upcoming regulator review and need to confirm a few things about Redwood's audit/access log exports for our tenant (Finvero):

1) What export formats do you support for access/audit traces (CSV, JSONL, Parquet)?
2) What's the maximum retention window exportable in a single run? Can we extract a full 36-month slice if needed, or does it need to be chunked?
3) For deletion requests, do you provide a tamper-evident proof of deletion or a signed attest? What does that package look like?
4) Are there options for secure transfer (SFTP, presigned S3 link, or direct FedRAMP-compliant transfer)?

If you can outline the delivery options and an estimated lead time, that would help us scope our compliance timeline.

Thanks,
Sam Taylor
Lead, Security Engineering
Finvero

--
Attachment: compliance_sample_request.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@finvero.co>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-16T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit trace export: formats / retention / deletion proof

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then a few clarifying Qs so we give you the exact artifacts you need: 

Summary answers (high level):
- Formats: CSV export by default for line-delimited records; JSONL and Parquet available on request for exports >10M rows.
- Window size: We can export up to 24 months in a single job. For >24 months we run chunked exports (configurable chunk size; default 30-day chunks to keep job stability).
- Deletion evidence: We provide a deletion package that contains a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums of exported files), a deletion-notice log (timestamped, signed by Redwood's export service), and a job execution trace showing the data slice removed. This is not yet a legal "certificate" but is accepted by many auditors.
- Transfer: Secure presigned S3 links (restricted IP + time), SFTP push, or direct SCP to an allowed customer endpoint. We can also deliver over an encrypted FedRAMP-compatible pipeline for enterprise contracts.

Couple of clarifying questions so Marissa/Ben and I can pick the right runbook:
1) Which exact date range do you want exported? (start/end).
2) Do you want a single consolidated schema (we'll canonicalize field names) or native-event format?
3) Do you require a signed deletion attest that includes a Redwood signatory name and timestamp? (that adds ~2 business days for legal review)

I'm attaching our short explainer (audit_export_options.pdf) and a small sample run output (runbook-export-sample.csv). Marissa/Ben — looping you in for SLA/cost details and to coordinate a run.

Best,
Hiro Tanaka
Manager, Security & Compliance (Redwood Inference)
hiro.tanaka@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

--
Attachments: audit_export_options.pdf, runbook-export-sample.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@finvero.co>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-17T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit trace export: formats / retention / deletion proof

Sam — hi, Marissa from Customer Ops. A few practical notes / next steps: 

- Lead time: For a single 24-month export we typically schedule 3 business days from request to delivery (includes verification & checksum signing). For requests that span >24 months (e.g., 36 months) expect 7-10 business days due to chunked job orchestration and QA.
- Cost: Large exports are billed as a one-time "export job" plus egress if using outbound transfer. I'll send a firm estimate once you confirm range and transfer method.
- Export slices: If you want a single consolidated file we will stitch the chunks and provide a manifest; however, very large consolidated files (>50GB) are delivered as chunked parts for reliability.
- Deletion evidence: We can produce a signed deletion package. Legal requires an explicit customer confirmation of the exact object IDs or the tenant range to be removed. Once we perform deletion, we provide the deletion package and a PGP-signed manifest.

Operational asks:
- Please provide target window and preferred transfer method. If S3 presigned is OK, include the destination bucket and allowed IPs. If you prefer SFTP, give us endpoint + SSH key.

I'll open a ticket in our runbook system and cc you on the schedule. Ben — can you confirm the SLA for FedRAMP pipeline delivery?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Operations Lead
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Sam — Ben here from Solutions/Security SLA. Short answers on the FedRAMP path and schedule: 

- FedRAMP delivery: available as an enterprise add-on (requires contract clause). If you already have enterprise terms in place (I see deal FINV-4821 in HubSpot) we can route export traffic over our FedRAMP-compliant transfer with HSM-backed signing. Otherwise presigned S3 with IP restrictions is the default.
- Timeline: With enterprise add-on, we can schedule a signed-run and deliver within 3 business days for up to 24 months. For 36 months (chunked), plan for 8 business days.
- Proof artifact: final package will include: (1) gzip'd export files; (2) signed manifest (SHA256) and job ID; (3) deletion_notice.json (PGP-signed); (4) execution_trace.log showing job steps and timestamps. We'll redact internal infrastructure identifiers when requested.

Sam — if you confirm the window (I assume 2024-01-01 -> 2026-12-31?) and transfer preference (S3 pref), we'll create a runbook ticket, attach an estimate, and propose run dates.

Regards,
